hormuz_disruption.label: Iran / Hormuz Disruption
hormuz_disruption.last_note: Ceasefire signals and Energy Secretary remarks about rising ship traffic pushed oil down hard today, introducing genuine de-escalation risk that could invalidate the disruption premium in oil and shipping insurance — but Iran shooting down a U.S. Apache helicopter the same day confirms the conflict remains live and fragile.

stagflation_regime.label: Stagflation Regime
stagflation_regime.last_note: CPI confirmed at 3.8% in April with May expected to print at 4.2%, the highest in nearly three years, while the Fed holds at 3.50 to 3.75% and market odds of a December rate hike have surged to 70% — a textbook stagflationary policy trap with oil-driven cost-push inflation layered on top of tariff pressure.

ai_bubble_risk.label: AI Bubble Risk Q4 2026
ai_bubble_risk.last_note: Hyperscaler capex is confirmed at $725 billion for 2026 with capital intensity at 45 to 57% of revenue and Morgan Stanley projecting $1.5 trillion in new tech sector debt over three years, while AI has yet to produce measurable GDP impact — the Anthropic IPO near $1 trillion valuation adds a late-cycle euphoria signal that pulls the trigger window closer to Q3 2026.

gold_supercycle.label: Gold Supercycle
gold_supercycle.last_note: Gold peaked above $5,400 in January 2026 and has since corrected sharply to $4,285 today as ceasefire signals reduce the geopolitical premium, stronger-than-expected jobs data lifts rate-hike odds, and the dollar strengthens — structural central bank demand provides a floor but the near-term technical setup is broken with tomorrow's CPI print the next critical pivot.

copper_deficit.label: Structural Copper Deficit
copper_deficit.last_note: Copper fell roughly 6% over the prior three sessions on hawkish Fed repricing and dollar strength but structural deficit conditions remain intact with concentrate shortages and limited new mine supply underpinning a 2026 average price forecast above $12,100 per metric ton, while US tariff deadlines continue to divert shipments and tighten supply outside the US.

nuclear_renaissance.label: Nuclear Renaissance
nuclear_renaissance.last_note: Meta signed agreements with Vistra, TerraPower, and Oklo to add 6.6 gigawatts of nuclear power by 2035 for its Prometheus AI supercluster, the DOE awarded $800 million to build SMRs in Tennessee and Michigan, and uranium spot prices have moved back above $100 per pound with tightening supply and renewed utility contracting — the AI power demand catalyst is accelerating faster than expected.

ALAB.note: The AI infrastructure connectivity thesis remains intact as Google and AWS alone are guiding for nearly $400 billion in combined 2026 capex and ALAB has strong hyperscaler design wins across PCIe, CXL, and Ethernet solutions, but at 20x forward price-to-sales and a price already above all analyst targets the thesis has not changed — the valuation has simply run too far ahead of it.

POWL.note: The data center electrical equipment thesis is structurally sound given the AI power buildout but 41x forward earnings and a PEG of 3.15 on only 6.5% revenue growth means POWL is pricing in perfection in a market where VIX has spiked 5% today and rate-hike risk is rising — the thesis is intact but the entry point is the problem.

MOD.note: The data center thermal management thesis is valid given that global data center electricity consumption is projected to double between 2022 and 2026, but negative FCF of minus $101M and a D/E of 48.23 creates acute balance sheet risk if rising rates compress the capex cycle, representing thesis drift from a growth story into a leverage story.

GFS.note: The CHIPS Act tailwind thesis for GlobalFoundries remains a show-me story with only 3.1% revenue growth and 6.8% ROE — the original thesis required CHIPS Act contract acceleration which has not materialized at scale, representing genuine thesis drift as the government spending catalyst has been slower than underwritten.

CRDO.note: Credo is delivering 272% year-over-year revenue growth in Q2 fiscal 2026, is acquiring DustPhotonics for $750 million to bring silicon photonics in-house, expects optical revenues to exceed $500 million in fiscal 2027, and has three confirmed hyperscaler customers with direct Anthropic relationships — the AI interconnect thesis is accelerating, not drifting, and CRDO trades at a lower forward price-to-sales of 14.98 versus ALAB at 20.26.

ARM.note: The royalty model and 97.5% gross margin thesis remain structurally brilliant and AI chip proliferation is expanding the royalty base, but at EV/EBITDA of 344 and 24% below its 52-week high with rate-hike risk rising sharply today, the margin of safety is insufficient and the stock is vulnerable to multiple compression before a better entry emerges.

S.note: SentinelOne is 28.8% below its 52-week high with negative operating margins of minus 28.8% and the cybersecurity consolidation wave led by Microsoft, Palo Alto Networks, and CrowdStrike is structurally compressing the addressable market for pure-play endpoint security — the original TAM expansion thesis has drifted into a market share erosion story.

ZS.note: Zscaler increased annual recurring revenue 26% year-over-year to over $3 billion with 52% free cash flow margin and has only 45% penetration of Fortune 500 companies suggesting significant runway, but the stock is 62.7% below its 52-week high and the negative EV/EBITDA reflects that the market has repriced the zero-trust premium — the business thesis is partially intact but the original growth premium valuation thesis is broken.

AXON.note: Axon is down 48.9% from its 52-week high with EV/EBITDA of 379 and only $63M FCF — the law enforcement tech thesis has not changed fundamentally but the drone warfare premium was speculative and has been aggressively de-rated, meaning the original entry thesis was based on narrative rather than demonstrated FCF generation, which constitutes thesis drift.

ISRG.note: Intuitive Surgical has zero debt, $4.5B cash, 23% revenue growth, and $2.3B FCF making it a genuine compounder, but at 36x forward earnings and 29.4% below highs the surgical robotics moat thesis is unchanged — the drift is purely valuation-related, not fundamental, and the stock remains a hold-not-add until the multiple contracts further.

RXRX.note: Recursion Pharmaceuticals has revenue growth of minus 56.1%, is burning $178M in FCF with negative operating margins of minus 1985%, and is 55.2% below its 52-week high — the original AI drug discovery thesis has collapsed as clinical pipeline progress has not justified the technology premium and this is now a capital destruction story with no near-term catalyst.

JEDI.note: The drone and modern warfare rearmament thesis is structurally intact given the Hormuz crisis has accelerated defense technology procurement, but at 25% below highs and with no fundamental data available for an ETF wrapper this remains a theme trade that requires a defined technical base before adding risk.

CWAN.note: Clearwater Analytics has 74.4% revenue growth and $160M FCF which is operationally compelling, but analyst targets of $24.47 to $24.55 against the current $24.35 price provide virtually zero upside consensus — at PEG of 10.24 and EV/EBITDA of 73.69 the institutional fintech thesis is fully priced with no margin of safety.

GRAB.note: Grab at $3.30 with $6.5B cash, 23.5% revenue growth, and PEG of 0.87 is the most asymmetric deep value setup in the portfolio on a pure fundamentals basis, but the stock is 50.2% below highs and the Southeast Asia super-app monetization thesis requires a specific catalyst such as a buyback announcement or profitability upgrade to unlock value — thesis intact, no trigger yet.
